You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def comps(g,bg):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]; out=[]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if g[r][c]!=bg and not seen[r][c]:
                st=[(r,c)]; seen[r][c]=True; cells=[]
                while st:
                    a,b=st.pop(); cells.append((a,b))
                    for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        x,y=a+dr,b+dc
                        if 0<=x<H and 0<=y<W and not seen[x][y] and g[x][y]!=bg:
                            seen[x][y]=True; st.append((x,y))
                out.append(cells)
    return out

def comps(g, bg=None):
    g=g if g else []
    seen=set(); res=[]
    for r in range(len(g)):
        for c in range(len(g[0])):
            if g[r][c]!=bg and (r,c) not in seen:
                st=[(r,c)]; comp=[]
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop()
                    if (y,x) in seen or not(0<=y<len(g)) or not(0<=x<len(g[0])) or g[y][x]==bg: continue
                    seen.add((y,x)); comp.append((y,x))
                    st+= [(y+1,x),(y-1,x),(y,x+1),(y,x-1)]
                res.append(comp)
    return res

def cluster_ops(I,O,bg):
    H=len(I);W=len(I[0])
    # 4-conn comps of non-bg
    seen=set(); cls=[]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if I[r][c]!=bg and (r,c) not in seen:
                st=[(r,c)];comp=set()
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop()
                    if (y,x) in comp or not(0<=y<H) or not(0<=x<W) or I[y][x]==bg: continue
                    comp.add((y,x)); st+=[(y+1,x),(y-1,x),(y,x+1),(y,x-1)]
                cls.append(comp)
    res={}
    for ci,comp in enumerate(cls):
        pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if O[r][c]!=bg and I[r][c]==bg and any(abs(r-y)+abs(c-x)==1 for y,x in comp)]
        res[ci]=(comp,pts)
    return res

def find_path(start, end, cells):
    # BFS over grid positions, only allowed to visit given cells, 4-dir
    if start in set(cells) and end not in set(cells): return None
    seen={start}; st=[start]
    while st:
        a=st.pop()
        if a==end: return [a]
        i,j=a
        for di,dj in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
            b=(i+di,j+dj)
            if b in cells and b not in seen:
                seen.add(b); st.append(b)
    return None
